ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The edges of a regular tetrahedron with vertices $A ,~ B,~ C$, and $D$ each have length one. Find the least possible distance between a pair of points $P$ and $Q$, where $P$ is on edge $AB$ and $Q$ is on edge $CD$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a regular tetrahedron, with vertices labeled A, B, C, D. Point P is located on edge AB, and point Q is located on edge CD; AB and CD do not share a vertex, so they are a pair of opposite edges in the tetrahedron. Reasoning: Place the tetrahedron according to a symmetric coordinate model. Let the midpoint of AB be the origin, and take A=(-1/2,0,0), B=(1/2,0,0). Place the opposite edge CD in a position parallel to the y-axis and with the same midpoint projection, and take C=(0,1/2,h), D=(0,-1/2,h). Because all edge lengths are 1, using AC=1 gives (1/2)^2+(1/2)^2+h^2=1, so h^2=1/2. Any point P on edge AB can be written as (s,0,0), and any point Q on edge CD can be written as (0,t,h), where s,t are both in [-1/2,1/2]. Thus PQ^2=(s-0)^2+(0-t)^2+(0-h)^2=s^2+t^2+h^2. Since h^2 is fixed, s^2+t^2 is minimized when s=t=0, so the shortest distance occurs between the midpoints of the two opposite edges. The minimum distance is h=√(1/2)=√2/2.

raw_record.question_text: The edges of a regular tetrahedron with vertices $A ,~ B,~ C$, and $D$ each have length one. Find the least possible distance between a pair of points $P$ and $Q$, where $P$ is on edge $AB$ and $Q$ is on edge $CD$.

method.method_draft: Use a symmetric coordinate model for the regular tetrahedron. From the diagram/text identify AB and CD as opposite edges, with P varying on AB and Q varying on CD. Place the midpoint of AB at the origin and set A=(-1/2,0,0), B=(1/2,0,0). Place the opposite edge CD parallel to the y-axis with the same midpoint projection, e.g. C=(0,1/2,h), D=(0,-1/2,h). Since every edge has length 1, impose AC=1: (1/2)^2+(1/2)^2+h^2=1, so h^2=1/2. A general point P on AB is (s,0,0) and a general point Q on CD is (0,t,h), with s,t in [-1/2,1/2]. Then PQ^2=s^2+t^2+h^2, minimized when s=t=0, i.e. at the midpoints of the two opposite edges. The minimum distance is h=sqrt(1/2)=sqrt(2)/2.
